provenance.citation: A. Newell and H. A. Simon, "GPS, A Program That Simulates Human Thought," RAND Corporation, P-2257, March 30, 1961 (Revised April 10, 1961). Presented at the Conference on Learning Automata, Karlsruhe, Germany, April 11–14, 1961.
provenance.locus: Fig. 3 (Methods for GPS — difference table) and Fig. 4 (Trace of GPS on First Part of Problem), pp. 3–15.
provenance.notes: GPS means-ends analysis: identify the first gap between current state and goal, find an operator that reduces that gap, apply it, recurse. The GPS breed engine operates on pred=val atoms — operator conclusions must contain the exact goal string as an add-effect. This fixture encodes a 2-step symbolic-logic transformation grounded from Fig. 4: current-expression=L1, target=L0; apply R6 to get L2 (horseshoe eliminated), then R12 to get L0 (double-negation removed). Each operator conclusion contains the exact goal atom it produces.

input.intent: transform propositional logic expression L1 into L0 using symbolic-logic rules

expected.note: GPS applies R6 to reduce the horseshoe-connective difference (L1→L2), then R12 to remove the double-negation (L2→L0). This matches the GPS trace in Fig. 4 of Newell & Simon P-2257: GPS first selects the delete-connective method (R6/R7 family), then the delete-sign method (R12 family) to reach L0.
